newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Eagle Star life and pensions business up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Eagle Star life and pensions business up in 1996.

text.p: Eagle Star said on Thursday that it has seen substantial increases in both its Irish life and pensions business in 1996.
Total new annual premium sales totalled 14.74 million Irish pounds, a rise of 29.2 percent on 1995, while total new single premium sales grew by 16 percent to 47.5 million punts.
Using normal industry weightings, this gives a combined annual premium equivalent growth of 25.7 percent, Eagle Star said in a statement.
The company said 1996 saw phenomenal growth in pensions.
Eagle Star's new annual premium pension business rose by 32.3 percent to 10.08 million while new single premium pensions increased by 29.5 percent to 36.2 million.

"Eagle Star intends to become the market leader in pensions by the year 2000 and we are confident that we have increased our market share significantly towards this goal in 1996," managing director Michael Brennan said. Eagle Star will also examine opportunities to further increase its pensions business by acquiring existing competitors where opportunities arise, he said.

The recovery in life product sales continued in 1996 with new annual life premium sales rising by 23 percent to 4.66 million while single premium unit-linked business reported a 96 percent increase to 9.0 million.
Eagle Star said this growth could be put down to investors' desire to get higher returns in a low interest rate, low inflation climate.
